newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber takes cue from Japan, ends up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber takes cue from Japan, ends up.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly higher on Wednesday in line with firmer Japanese prices and mild shortcovering in the market, dealers said.
"We marked the prices slightly up after Japanese prices rose. There was also some slight shortcovering in the local market," a local rubber trader said.
Tokyo and Kobe's benchmark April contract climbed 2.9 yen to end at 144.0, respectively.
"It was quiet. The only reason prices went up was really the Japanese. On our part, we did a bit of the December contract for RSS3 rubber at 126 (U.S. cents a kg)," a dealer said.
Traders said the market largely discounted reports of a fall in Japanese rubber stocks with one dealer saying "we need to see a bigger fall before getting excited about it."
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 126.00-126.25 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 126.25 cents.
December RSS1 was seen at 180.50-182.50 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.29) a kg against 180.50 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 178.00-180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from 178.50 cents.
